# Release lifecycle

98 records support this lifecycle stage.

- [ACR-SyncTool](https://github.com/IvanJosipovic/ACR-SyncTool) — Command-line tool for synchronizing container images into Azure Container Registry.
- [AKS Kargo AnalysisRun logs](https://github.com/IvanJosipovic/aks-kargo-analysisrun-logs) — API service exposing Azure Log Analytics job logs through Kargo's AnalysisRun log interface.

- [Artifact Hub](https://artifacthub.io) — Discover and share packages (Helm charts, operators, etc.).
- [Buildah](https://buildah.io) — Daemonless OCI image-building CLI and library, with Dockerfile and scripted workflows; complementary to the Podman container runtime.
- [BuildKit](https://docs.docker.com/build/buildkit) — Moby build-execution toolkit and backend for concurrent, cache-efficient builds, used by Docker Buildx and other clients.
- [Bunnyshell](https://www.bunnyshell.com) — Environment-as-a-service platform for preview, staging, and ephemeral cloud environments driven by environment-as-code workflows.

- [Cloudsmith](https://cloudsmith.com/) — Managed multi-format package and artifact repository service with access controls and supply-chain features.
- [ContainerYard](https://github.com/mcmah309/containeryard) — Tool for composing reusable modules into generated Containerfiles.
- [Convox](https://www.convox.com) — Platform for deploying and managing containers.
- [Cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign) — Sigstore CLI for signing and verifying container images, other artifacts and attestations using identity-based or self-managed keys; Fulcio, Rekor, sigstore-go and policy-controller are separate components.
- [DeepEval](https://deepeval.com/) — Local-first framework for evaluating and regression-testing LLM applications, agents, RAG pipelines, and MCP systems.
- [Dependency-Track](https://dependencytrack.org) — OWASP component-analysis platform that continuously evaluates software bills of materials and supply-chain risk.
- [Devtron](https://devtron.ai) — Kubernetes application-delivery platform with an Apache-2.0 core, CI/CD and Helm/GitOps integrations, plus separately offered commercial platform capabilities.
- [dist (cargo-dist)](https://github.com/axodotdev/cargo-dist) — Release automation for building and distributing application binaries and installers.
- [Distroless](https://github.com/GoogleContainerTools/distroless) — Minimal runtime container images without a shell or package manager in standard variants; separately published debug variants support troubleshooting.
- [Docker](https://www.docker.com) — Product ecosystem for developing, building, distributing, and running application containers.
- [Docker Build](https://docs.docker.com/build/) — Documentation umbrella for Docker image building: Buildx is the CLI client and BuildKit its execution backend; not a separate source repository or licence grant.
- [Docker Buildx](https://github.com/docker/buildx) — Docker CLI build client for BuildKit, supporting configurable builders, multi-platform images and external build caches.
- [Docker Hardened Images](https://hub.docker.com/hardened-images/catalog) — Docker-maintained catalog of minimal, hardened container images, Helm charts, and system packages with community and paid tiers.

- [Dokku](https://dokku.com) — PaaS for deploying apps using Docker.
- [Earthly](https://earthly.dev) — Dockerfile-like build orchestration CLI; upstream ended active OSS maintenance in April 2025 and retired its Cloud/Satellite services in July 2025.
- [Flux](https://fluxcd.io) — Open and extensible GitOps toolkit for Kubernetes.
- [Flux Operator](https://fluxoperator.dev) — ControlPlane-maintained Kubernetes operator installing, configuring and upgrading Flux CD instances through FluxInstance resources, with additional self-service APIs. Its AGPL-3.0 software is separate from Flux CD core and commercial ControlPlane distribution/support terms.
- [flux9s](https://flux9s.ca) — Terminal UI for inspecting Flux GitOps controllers and Kubernetes workloads, with RBAC-gated cluster operations.
- [git push no-mistakes](https://kunchenguid.github.io/no-mistakes/) — Local Git push gate that validates changes in an isolated worktree before publishing a branch and opening a pull request.

- [GitOps Bridge](https://github.com/gitops-bridge-dev/gitops-bridge) — GitOps Bridge is a community pattern and example repository passing cluster-provisioning metadata from IaC to GitOps-managed Kubernetes addons and workloads. Its Terraform/Argo CD example is described as stable; Flux integration is listed as in progress, not universal executable-platform support.
- [GoCD](https://www.gocd.org) — Apache-2.0 continuous-delivery server with agents, pipeline dependencies, materials and value-stream visibility; plugins and support terms remain separate.

- [Husky](https://typicode.github.io/husky) — Node.js Git hooks manager that installs project-local scripts for pre-commit and other Git lifecycle events.
- [JayeX (formerly Jenkins X)](https://jayex.io/) — JayeX, formerly Jenkins X, is a Kubernetes CI/CD and GitOps tool suite using Tekton and Lighthouse, with the Apache-2.0 jx CLI and separately maintained components.
- [Jenkins](https://www.jenkins.io) — MIT-licensed Jenkins automation server for controller/agent CI/CD pipelines, with independently licensed plugins and operator-managed execution infrastructure.

- [JFrog Connect](https://jfrog.com/connect/) — Commercial IoT and edge-device management component of the JFrog Platform for fleet monitoring and OTA software delivery.

- [JFrog Platform](https://jfrog.com/platform/) — Commercial software supply-chain platform unifying artifact and AI asset management, security, governance, and release delivery.
- [Kamal](https://kamal-deploy.org) — Deploy and roll containerized web applications onto remote servers over SSH using Kamal and kamal-proxy, without requiring Kubernetes.
- [Kargo](https://kargo.io) — GitOps promotion workflow for Kubernetes.
- [Keel](https://keel.sh) — Automated Kubernetes deployment updates.

- [Kubesearch](https://kubesearch.dev) — Search engine for Helm charts and Kubernetes packages.

- [Nix](https://nixos.org) — Functional, reproducible package manager and build system; distinct from NixOS/nixpkgs and not a standalone OCI image builder.

- [Piku](https://piku.github.io) — Heroku-like mini PaaS.
- [Porter](https://github.com/porter-dev) — Porter cloud platform for deploying applications into user-owned Kubernetes clusters; current commercial and source-licence boundaries require review.
- [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com) — Multi-language Git hook framework using declarative configuration and managed hook environments for repeatable local or CI checks.

- [Uncloud](https://uncloud.run) — Deploy and operate containerized workloads across Docker hosts with service discovery and HTTPS ingress, without a Kubernetes control plane.
- [Vercel](https://vercel.com/) — Managed web application platform providing Git-based builds, preview deployments, production hosting, and serverless infrastructure.
